home.title: Prospekt: lens simulator for iPhone. See what any lens frames on your camera
home.description: Prospekt is an iPhone lens simulator: a live viewfinder that shows what a 14 to 300 mm lens frames on your camera body. 59 bodies, {price} once, works offline.
home.h1: See what any lens frames on your camera, before you buy it
home.lead: Prospekt is an iPhone app that turns your phone into a viewfinder for a lens you don't own yet. Pick your camera body and a focal length from 14 to 300 mm, point the phone, and see the framing live.
home.facts: {price} once. No subscription, no account, no ads. Works offline.
home.hero_caption: What 24, 35, 50 and 85 mm frame on a full-frame camera, drawn over a photo taken at 14 mm.
home.for_1: You're choosing between a 35 mm and a 50 mm, or a 50 and an 85, and want to see the difference before you spend the money.
home.for_2: You have an APS-C or Micro Four Thirds camera and crop factor still confuses you.
home.for_3: You're scouting a location and want to know if your 24-70 is wide enough, or if you need the 70-200.
home.for_4: You're switching systems and want to know what your old lenses become on the new body.
home.for_5: You're learning photography and want to feel what focal lengths look like.
home.how_1: Pick your camera body. 59 are built in, from Canon, Sony, Nikon, Fujifilm, Panasonic, OM System, Leica, Hasselblad, Pentax and Sigma. You can add your own with any crop factor.
home.how_2: Turn the wheel to a focal length from 14 to 300 mm. It clicks at the popular ones. Add a 1.4x or 2x extender if you use one.
home.how_3: Point your iPhone. Prospekt switches between the ultra-wide, wide and telephoto cameras and sets the zoom so the frame matches that lens on that body.
home.how_4: Take a snapshot. It's saved with a watermark showing the focal length, crop factor, full-frame equivalent and aspect ratio (3:2, 4:3, 16:9 or 1:1), so you can compare later.
home.price_includes: Everything: all 59 bodies, your own bodies, extenders, four aspect ratios, snapshots and future updates. No subscription, no in-app purchases, no ads.
home.price_note: Price in the US App Store. Other countries pay the local equivalent.
home.privacy_text: Prospekt collects no data. There is no account, no analytics, no ads and no third-party code. The camera picture stays on your iPhone, and a photo is saved only when you tap the shutter, to your own photo library.
home.limits_1: It shows framing, not background blur. The bokeh of an f/1.4 lens is not simulated.
home.limits_2: Your iPhone's widest camera sets the widest framing you can preview: about 13 mm full-frame equivalent on iPhones with an ultra-wide camera.
home.limits_3: At long focal lengths the iPhone uses digital zoom, so the picture gets soft. The framing is still right.
home.limits_4: Perspective comes from where you stand, not from the lens. Prospekt shows the framing from where you are standing.
home.limits_5: iPhone only, iOS 17 or later. No Android or iPad version.
home.compare_live_calc: No, a sample photo or a diagram
home.compare_cost_rent: A rental fee and a deposit
home.compare_note: Calculator sites are free and fine for quick numbers, our own lens comparison tool included. Renting is the only way to see bokeh and how a lens renders. Prospekt sits in between: the real scene, your body, a one-time price.
home.faq_1_q: Is there an app that shows what a lens will look like before I buy it?
home.faq_1_a: Yes. Prospekt shows the framing of any focal length from 14 to 300 mm on your camera body, live through your iPhone camera. It costs {price} once on the App Store.
home.faq_2_q: How can I see the difference between 35 mm, 50 mm and 85 mm?
home.faq_2_a: Pick your body in Prospekt and turn the wheel between the three while you point at the same scene. Without the app, compare them over a sample photo in our free lens comparison tool.
home.faq_3_q: What does a 50 mm lens look like on APS-C?
home.faq_3_a: It frames like a 75 mm lens on full frame, or 80 mm on Canon APS-C, which is a short telephoto. Every body has its own table on the camera pages.
home.faq_4_a: It's how much smaller your sensor is than full frame, measured across the diagonal. Multiply a focal length by it to get the full-frame equivalent: 35 mm on a 1.5x body frames like 52.5 mm.
home.faq_5_a: Yes. It never needs the internet, and there's no account to sign in to.
home.faq_6_q: Does it simulate depth of field or background blur?
home.faq_6_a: No. It shows what the lens frames, which is what decides most lens purchases. Bokeh depends on the aperture, the distance and the lens design, and a phone can't show it honestly.
home.faq_7_a: 59 bodies from 10 brands are built in, across full frame, APS-C, Micro Four Thirds and medium format. For any other camera, add it with its crop factor.
home.faq_8_a: No. You pay {price} once and every update is included.
home.faq_9_a: nakolini, a two-person studio: Vitalii Kikot and Dmytro Hryb. We also make Anonimo and Expenny.
tool.title: Lens comparison tool: see what any focal length frames on your camera
tool.description: Free lens comparison tool. Pick your camera and focal lengths or a zoom, see the framing over a photo and how far to stand for a portrait. Full-frame equivalent and angle of view for 59 cameras.
tool.h1: Lens comparison: see what each focal length frames on your camera
tool.lead: Pick your camera and the focal lengths or zoom you're deciding between. The frames show what each lens would capture from the same spot, and the table shows how much it covers and how far to stand. Use one of our sample photos or your own; your photo never leaves your browser.
tool.focals_label: Focal lengths (tap to add or remove)
tool.photo_focal_label: Your photo's focal length, 35 mm equivalent
tool.photo_focal_hint: Found in the photo's details. The iPhone ultra-wide (0.5x) is about 13 mm, the main camera about 24 to 26 mm.
tool.photo_private: Your photo stays on your device. Nothing is uploaded.
tool.preview_hint: Tap a focal length in the table to see its frame up close.
tool.soft_note: Long focal lengths are cropped from a wide photo, so they look soft here. The framing is right.
tool.noscript: The interactive tool needs JavaScript. The figure and tables below work without it.
tool.static_caption: On a full-frame camera from the same spot: 24, 35, 50 and 85 mm drawn over a photo taken at 14 mm.
tool.equiv_title: The same framing on different sensors
tool.equiv_intro: To frame like a full-frame lens on a smaller or bigger sensor, divide by the crop factor. The table shows the focal length you need on each format.
tool.math_1: A lens frames like its focal length times the crop factor on full frame. That number is the full-frame equivalent.
tool.math_2: The angle of view is 2 x arctan(sensor size / (2 x focal length)), for the width, the height or the diagonal of the sensor.
tool.math_3: Frames are drawn on a flat (rectilinear) projection, which is how all normal lenses draw. Fisheye lenses are different.
tool.math_4: Micro Four Thirds and 44 x 33 medium format sensors are 4:3, so their frames are taller than the 3:2 frames of full frame and APS-C.
tool.faq_1_q: How do I compare two lenses without buying them?
tool.faq_1_a: Pick your camera above and tap both focal lengths. The frames show what each one captures from the same spot. To see it on a real scene, Prospekt does the same live through your iPhone.
tool.faq_2_q: Is 35 mm or 50 mm better for everyday photos?
tool.faq_2_a: 35 mm shows more of the scene and suits streets, travel and small rooms. 50 mm is tighter and suits portraits and details. Compare both frames on your camera above and pick the one closer to how you see.
tool.faq_3_q: Does the tool work on a phone?
tool.faq_3_a: Yes. It runs in any modern browser, and your own photos are processed on your device.
tool.faq_4_q: How far away do I stand for a full-body portrait?
tool.faq_4_a: On a full-frame camera held vertically, about {d35} with a 35 mm lens, {d50} with 50 mm, {d85} with 85 mm and {d135} with 135 mm. That fits a 1.8 m person in 90% of the frame height. Every camera page lists these distances for that body.
tool.math_5: Coverage at a distance is the distance x sensor size / focal length. It assumes the lens is focused far away. Close up, most lenses frame a little tighter.
tool.zooms_label: Zoom lenses (tap to add both ends)
tool.subject_hint: The subject fills 90% of the frame height. A standing adult is about 1.8 m (6 ft), head and shoulders about 0.5 m (1.6 ft).
tool.distance_note: Covers is the width x height of the scene with the camera held horizontally. Close up, real lenses frame a little tighter than these numbers.
tool.distance_title: What each focal length covers at a distance
tool.distance_intro: On a full-frame camera held horizontally, each lens captures a scene this wide and this tall. On a smaller sensor, use the focal length with the same full-frame look from the table above. 1 m is about 3.3 ft.
tool.portrait_title: How far to stand for a portrait
tool.portrait_intro: On a full-frame camera held vertically, with the subject filling 90% of the frame height. Full body means a 1.8 m person, head and shoulders about 0.5 m.
tool.portrait_row: {focal}: about {full} for a full-body portrait, {head} for head and shoulders.

body.title: {body} lens simulator: what each focal length frames
body.description: What 14 to 300 mm lenses frame on the {body} ({format}, {crop} crop factor): full-frame equivalent, angle of view and a framing chart.
body.intro: The {body} has a {crop} crop factor ({format} sensor), so a lens frames like its focal length times {crop} on full frame. A 50 mm lens on the {body} frames like {equiv_50} on full frame.
body.intro_ff: The {body} has a full-frame sensor, so every lens frames exactly as marked. A 50 mm lens on the {body} frames like 50 mm, with a horizontal angle of view of {h_50}.
body.note_leica_q3: The Q3 has a fixed 28 mm lens, so you cannot change lenses. Its digital crop modes frame like 35, 50, 75 and 90 mm, and the table shows what those look like.
body.frames_title: How the frames nest on the {body}
body.frames_caption: Frames of 24, 35, 50, 85 and 135 mm lenses on the {body}, from the same spot. The outer frame is 24 mm.
body.classic_intro: To get the framing a full-frame shooter means by these focal lengths, use these on the {body}:
body.classic_row: To frame like {equiv} on full frame, use {focal} on the {body}.
body.same_format: Other cameras with the same sensor size
body.open_tool: Compare focal lengths on the {body} over a photo
body.faq_1_q: What does a 50 mm lens look like on the {body}?
body.faq_1_a: It frames like {equiv_50} on full frame, with a horizontal angle of view of {h_50}.
body.faq_2_q: Which lens gives a 50 mm full-frame look on the {body}?
body.faq_2_a: A lens of about {focal_for_50}. It frames like 50 mm on full frame.
body.faq_3_q: Can I see these focal lengths on the {body} before buying a lens?
body.faq_3_a: Yes. Prospekt for iPhone has the {body} built in. Pick it, choose a focal length and point your phone to see the framing live.
body.faq_4_q: How far do I stand for a full-body portrait with an 85 mm lens on the {body}?
body.faq_4_a: About {full_85} from the subject, with the camera held vertically. That fits a 1.8 m person in 90% of the frame height. For head and shoulders, stand about {head_85} away.
body.faq_5_q: How much does a 35 mm lens cover at 3 m on the {body}?
body.faq_5_a: About {cover_35_3}, width by height, with the camera held horizontally. At 10 m it covers about {cover_35_10}.
body.distance_title: What each lens covers at a distance on the {body}
body.distance_intro: Width x height of the scene each focal length captures on the {body}, held horizontally. Close up, real lenses frame a little tighter than this.
body.portrait_intro: How far to stand from the subject with the {body} held vertically, so the subject fills 90% of the frame height. Full body means a 1.8 m person, head and shoulders about 0.5 m.
body.portrait_row: With {focal} on the {body}: about {full} for a full-body portrait, {head} for head and shoulders.
